newsitem.title: UK: BT TAKES LARGE HIT AS STOCK GOES EX-DIV. [CORRECTED 12:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: BT TAKES LARGE HIT AS STOCK GOES EX-DIV. [CORRECTED 12:41 GMT]

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications fell sharply on Monday in active trade as the stock went ex-dividend.
The dividend payout deducted comprised an 11.95p per share final dividend and a special dividend of 35p.
The shares duly fell 47-1/2p to 379p, making BT the biggest percentage loser in the London market and one of the most actively traded stocks.
BT is one of the most heavily-weighted stocks in the FTSE, and the effect of the sharp decline in its share price was to take about 18 points off the blue-chip index.
The shares were also dogged by uncertainty surrounding BT's planned merger with MCI and intense press speculation over whether the deal will be successful.
"Obviously everybody is waiting to see what will happen with the merger and until that's cleared up the shares will suffer," said James Saltiel at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
BT stock is now trading at a similar level to before the MCI merger announcement.

In the weekend press, reports suggested that BT was likely to launch a six billion stg share buyback if the merger failed. Newspapers also speculated that some of BT's biggest investors were opposed to the MCI bid.
Analysts said they hoped that the British telecoms giant would complete its review of the proposed deal by the end of this month.
